sources.quote: Implicit caching directly passes cache cost savings to developers without the need to create an explicit cache. Now, when you send a request to one of the Gemini 2.5 models, if the request shares a common prefix as one of previous requests, then it’s eligible for a cache hit. We will dynamically pass cost savings back to you, providing the same 75% token discount.
sources.supports: Google says Gemini 2.5 implicit cache hits receive a 75% discount; against the $1.25 input rate that is $0.3125/M tokens, rounded to $0.31.

sources.quote: | Input price | Free of charge | $1.25, prompts \<= 200k tokens $2.50, prompts \> 200k tokens |
sources.supports: Google's published Gemini 2.5 Pro input price is $1.25/M tokens for prompts up to 200k tokens, the basis for the discounted cached token price.

sources.quote: | Output price (including thinking tokens) | Free of charge | $10.00, prompts \<= 200k tokens $15.00, prompts \> 200k |
sources.supports: Google's published Gemini 2.5 Pro output price is $10/M tokens for prompts up to 200k tokens.

sources.quote: The growth and demand for Gemini 2.5 Pro continues to be the steepest of any of our models we have ever seen. To allow more customers to build on this model in production, we are making the 06-05 version of the model stable, with the same pareto frontier price point as before.
sources.supports: Google says the successor model retained the prior price point; this is corroborating context that the catalog's $1.25/$10 base rates were not a pricing increase.

notes: The $0.31 cache_read amount follows from Google's 75% implicit-caching discount applied to $1.25 input pricing ($0.3125, rounded). This indicates the earlier models.dev omission was a catalog error, not a newly effective provider price. The announcement copy gives no effective date, and the Internet Archive CDX request returned 503, so no date or snapshot bracket can be established.
